name: Diana Harshbarger
bio: Two-term incumbent first elected 2020. Trump-endorsed; expected to win re-nomination handily.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: Supports school choice and state/parental control over education; no direct Head Start or pre-K funding position; co-sponsored Parents Bill of Rights Act; delivers books to early learning centers in district.
early_childhood_ed.details: Harshbarger's education stance centers on parental rights and state control. She co-sponsored the Parents Bill of Rights Act and cited the June 2025 SCOTUS ruling affirming parental opt-out rights as a victory. Her office participates in the U.S. Library of Congress Surplus Books Program, delivering books to childcare and early learning centers across East Tennessee, including the First Tennessee Human Resource Agency and Jefferson County schools. No new 2026 legislation or floor statements specifically addressing federal early childhood education funding or Head Start were found.

child_hunger.summary: Voted YES on the Nutritious SNAP Act 2025 and YES on the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 (H.R. 7567, April 30, 2026), which preserves $187B in SNAP cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. CDF 'F' rating from 117th Congress.
child_hunger.details: Harshbarger voted YES on the 2026 Farm Bill (H.R. 7567), which passed 224-200 on April 30, 2026. The bill preserves all SNAP cuts enacted via the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025), including new work requirements for parents of children 14 and older and adults up to age 64. Democrats' floor amendments to reverse SNAP cuts were defeated. Tennessee saw roughly 97,000 people cut from SNAP since the OBBBA took effect. No public statement from Harshbarger specifically addressing child hunger or Summer EBT in Tennessee was found in May-June 2026.

parental_support.summary: Introduced the STOP Act (H.R. 8573, April 29, 2026) banning gender transition procedures on minors with $100K civil penalties and a private right of action for parents. Previously voted YES on HR 7024 (expanded CTC, Jan 2024). Co-sponsored Parents Bill of Rights Act.
parental_support.details: On April 29, 2026, Harshbarger introduced the Safeguarding the Overall Protection of Minors (STOP) Act (H.R. 8573) alongside Sen. Roger Marshall. The bill prohibits gender transition procedures on minors under 18, imposes civil penalties of at least $100,000 per violation, and creates a private right of action for 'victims of gender transition procedures — or their parent, guardian, or caretaker if the victim was still a minor.' It also establishes a federal Victims Compensation Fund. She stated: 'As a pharmacist and a mother, protecting patients — especially children — has always been my top priority.' No new positions on paid family leave, childcare costs, or child tax credit were found in May-June 2026.

name: Kristi Burke
bio: Democratic primary candidate from East Tennessee.
photo_credit: Direct headshot URL not found; campaign uses logo imagery

early_childhood_ed.summary: Supports public school funding with explicitly stated access 'from early childhood through higher education.' States 'public dollars must go to public schools.' No specific pre-K or Head Start funding position stated publicly.
early_childhood_ed.details: Burke's campaign platform explicitly includes early childhood in her education plank, stating access must begin at the early childhood level. She affirms 'public dollars must go to public schools' and frames education as essential to 'opportunity, economic mobility, and a functioning democracy.' She spoke at a March 2026 Democratic rally calling for fully funded public education. At a May 2026 Greene County Democratic Party meeting, she stated she would 'direct more funding towards education.' No specific policy proposals on Head Start, childcare subsidies, or pre-K program funding were found.

child_hunger.summary: Stated at a March 2026 rally that 'no child should ever go hungry.' No specific SNAP, Summer EBT, or food program policy positions identified. No new statements found in June 2026.
child_hunger.details: No new policy statements on child hunger, SNAP, Summer EBT, or federal food programs were found for Burke in May or June 2026. Her campaign platform focuses on cost of living, shifting tax burdens off working families, cheaper healthcare access, and fair wages, but does not articulate specific food assistance positions. The existing note from the March 2026 rally ('no child should ever go hungry') remains the most specific statement on record.

parental_support.summary: No specific positions identified on paid family/medical leave, child tax credit, childcare costs, or TANF. Supports fair wages and cost-of-living relief for working families broadly.
parental_support.details: Burke's campaign platform and all available May-June 2026 sources do not include specific positions on paid family and medical leave, the child tax credit, childcare affordability, or TANF. Her general platform supports workers being 'empowered,' fair wages, and shifting tax burdens off working families. She frames herself as a community advocate who believes in 'a Tennessee where healthcare is a right, workers are empowered, and every one of us has the freedom to live with integrity.' No specific parental support policy proposals were found.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific position on early childhood education or childcare. Campaign focus is on healthcare access, food insecurity, protecting children from gun violence, and union support.
early_childhood_ed.details: Garcia's campaign focus, as stated at the May 2026 Greene County Democratic Party meeting, centers on protecting children from gun violence, addressing food insecurity, expanding healthcare access, and supporting unions and police reform. No statements on pre-K, Head Start, childcare subsidies, or early education funding were identified. His background as a small business owner and Army veteran is prominent in his campaign messaging.

child_hunger.summary: Explicitly listed addressing food insecurity as a top campaign priority at the May 2026 Greene County Democratic Party meeting. No specific SNAP, Summer EBT, or food program policy positions articulated.
child_hunger.details: At the May 2026 Greene County Democratic Party primary candidates meeting, Garcia specifically named food insecurity as one of his top campaign priorities, alongside protecting children from gun violence and expanding healthcare access. No policy specifics on SNAP, Summer EBT, WIC, school meals, or other federal food programs were found. His broader messaging references rising grocery, fuel, and utility costs squeezing working families in East Tennessee.

parental_support.summary: No position on paid family/medical leave, child tax credit, childcare costs, or TANF. Focus on rising cost of living squeezing working families and expanding healthcare access.
parental_support.details: No specific parental support policy positions were found for Garcia in May-June 2026. At candidate forums, Garcia focused on healthcare access, food insecurity, gun safety for children, and union support. No statements on paid leave, CTC, TANF, or childcare affordability were identified.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No public position found on early childhood education; platform focuses on healthcare, government accountability, and constituent representation.
early_childhood_ed.details: Kerr's campaign website lists policy positions under several headings — Government Accountability, Healthcare, Women's Health, Gun Reform, Veteran Issues, and Economic Focus — but does not include an education section or any mention of early childhood programs. No new June 2026 statements found.

child_hunger.summary: No public position found on child hunger, SNAP, school meals, or child nutrition programs.
child_hunger.details: Kerr's publicly available campaign platform covers healthcare access and working family economic concerns but does not specifically address child hunger, SNAP benefits, school meal programs, or child nutrition reauthorization. His platform states he will 'support initiatives that benefit working families and rural economies.' No new June 2026 statements found.

parental_support.summary: No public position found on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, or childcare costs; supports 'working families' broadly and maternal care access.
parental_support.details: Kerr's Women's Health section supports 'family planning and maternal care' access, and his Economic Focus section pledges to 'support initiatives that benefit working families,' but these references do not translate into specific positions on paid family leave legislation, Child Tax Credit expansion, or federal childcare subsidy programs. As a father of two who served 20 years in the Marines, family issues are part of his personal story. No new June 2026 statements found.

name: Tim Burchett
bio: Three-term incumbent serving since 2019. Outspoken populist conservative; minimal primary opposition.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: 26% support / 74% oppose on education bills per GovTrack; no pre-K or Head Start position; CDF 'F' rating 117th Congress; reintroduced BLOCK Act (H.R. 847, Feb 2025) to prevent school grants based on political ideology.
early_childhood_ed.details: No new Burchett statements or votes specifically on early childhood education or childcare were found in May-June 2026. His 2026 education activity remains focused on K-12 issues: he reintroduced H.R. 847 (BLOCK Act) in February 2025 to block federal school grants tied to political ideology. His official education page does not address pre-K or childcare. He chairs the DOGE oversight subcommittee (appointed January 2026).

child_hunger.summary: Voted YES on One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025) cutting SNAP by ~$187B; on April 27, 2026 announced plans to propose SNAP soda ban amendment; visited Second Harvest Food Bank amid rising food insecurity in East Tennessee (202,000 food-insecure residents, up 12,000 year-over-year). Tennessee cutting ~97,000 people from SNAP; SNAP obligations projected to nearly triple from $56.7M to $165.3M annually.
child_hunger.details: Burchett voted YES on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, then on April 27, 2026 posted on X announcing plans to present a farm bill amendment banning soft drinks from SNAP, citing child Type 2 diabetes prevalence. Tennessee residents and advocates pushed back, noting it stigmatizes low-income families. He visited Second Harvest Food Bank of East Tennessee, which now serves 202,000 food-insecure people across 18 counties, up 12,000 from the prior year. Tennessee SNAP obligations are projected to surge from $56.7M to $165.3M annually. His office stated: 'The federal government will continue providing $685 million to Tennessee in SNAP benefits... Making thoughtful changes today will help secure a strong and prosperous future for our children.'

parental_support.summary: Voted YES on HR 7024 (Feb 2024, expanded CTC); co-sponsored HR 7925 (April 2026) limiting TANF for non-citizens; chairs DOGE oversight subcommittee (Jan 2026). In May 2026 warned fellow Republicans that the party 'has a real problem' on affordability messaging.
parental_support.details: Burchett's April 2026 co-sponsorship of H.R. 7925 limits TANF eligibility for non-citizens. He chairs the DOGE oversight subcommittee focused on reducing government spending. In May 2026, Burchett warned fellow Republicans that the party 'has a real problem' on affordability messaging after a narrow special election result in Tennessee, stating: 'We do a terrible job of messaging.' No specific new positions on paid family/medical leave, childcare affordability, or CTC expansion were found in May-June 2026.

name: Michaela Barnett
bio: Democratic challenger; previous experience working in Congress.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Explicitly supports affordable childcare as a campaign priority; no specific pre-K or Head Start positions found. General education investment stance includes STEM, trade schools, and public schools.
early_childhood_ed.details: Barnett's platform explicitly calls for 'affordable childcare' and 'paid parental leave' as core priorities (confirmed via grassroots candidate interview, May 2026). She supports investing in STEM education, trade schools, and public schools while opposing policies that strip resources from public education. No specific position on federal pre-K, Head Start, or CCDBG found. Her Campbell County speech referenced 'affordable healthy food' in a workforce investment context.

child_hunger.summary: Cites OBBB's 'devastating consequences in East Tennessee'; supports affordable healthy food access; no specific SNAP/WIC proposals found. Food insecurity framing tied to cost-of-living and federal cuts.
child_hunger.details: Barnett has cited the One Big Beautiful Bill's impacts on East Tennessee, including consequences related to food access and healthcare. She frames food affordability as part of broader economic dignity — her platform references 'affordable healthy food' and the harm of federal cuts to working families. East Tennessee has the highest pregnancy-related death rate in the state at 73 per 100,000 live births, a context she connects to the broader impact of OBBB cuts. No specific SNAP restoration proposals, WIC expansion positions, or school meals stances found in May-June 2026 searches.

parental_support.summary: Explicitly supports affordable childcare and paid parental leave. Frames reproductive freedom and maternal healthcare as family support issues, noting Tennessee has one of the nation's highest maternal mortality rates — East Tennessee's rate is 73 per 100,000 live births. No specific CTC or PFML dollar figures stated.
parental_support.details: Confirmed via grassroots candidate interview: Barnett explicitly advocates for 'paid parental leave' and 'affordable childcare' as campaign pillars. She also highlights rebuilding maternal healthcare infrastructure, noting Tennessee has one of the nation's highest maternal mortality rates. She frames opposition to OBBB cuts through the lens of harm to working families. No specific child tax credit expansion figure or federal paid family and medical leave dollar/week amounts stated. Her platform also includes housing and healthcare as connected family support issues.

name: Chuck Fleischmann
bio: Eight-term incumbent and Chattanooga attorney. $4.1M cash on hand; expected easy re-nomination.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: Opposes federal education mandates; voted against ARP childcare/pre-K funding; supports OBBB which includes enhanced employer childcare tax credits but no direct federal pre-K investment. Co-sponsored legislation to protect parental rights regarding in-person schooling and COVID vaccine decisions.
early_childhood_ed.details: No new May-June 2026 statements specifically on early childhood education found. Fleischmann's long-standing position opposes federal involvement in education. He voted NO on ARP (2021) and against Build Back Better childcare/pre-K provisions. His vote for OBBB (final passage July 2025) increased the employer-provided childcare tax credit from 25% to 40% (up to $500K/year cap) but did not fund federal pre-K or Head Start expansions. He co-sponsored legislation to keep children in classrooms and codify parental rights regarding COVID-19 vaccination decisions. His FY23 appropriations request included $2.5M for an Athens-McMinn YMCA Early Learning Center, showing some district-level childcare funding support. Trump endorsed him for 2026.

child_hunger.summary: Voted against the American Rescue Plan's expanded child nutrition provisions and supported the One Big Beautiful Bill, which is projected to cut approximately $283 million in SNAP from Hamilton County (Chattanooga area) over a decade. Fleischmann's OBBB statement did not address SNAP impacts.
child_hunger.details: Fleischmann voted YES on OBBB (final passage July 4, 2025). His public statement on the bill emphasized tax cuts, border security, energy, and defense — he did not address SNAP cuts or their impact on Tennessee families. OBBB cuts approximately $187-200B from SNAP nationally over 10 years; expands work requirements to adults 55-64 and parents of children 14+; shifts administrative cost burden to 75% state starting FY2027. Urban Institute estimated 3.3 million families with children would see average benefit cuts. Tennessee's 700,000 SNAP-eligible children are already without Summer EBT in summer 2026. He voted NAY on the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Roll Call 72).

parental_support.summary: Supported 2017 TCJA CTC ($2,000); voted against 2021 ARP CTC expansion; voted for OBBB which raised CTC to $2,200 and permanently enhanced employer childcare and paid leave credits. Co-sponsored Protecting Parental Rights Act. Does not support federal PFML mandate.
parental_support.details: OBBB — which Fleischmann strongly supported — made the $2,200 child tax credit permanent (indexed to inflation from 2026), enhanced the employer-provided childcare credit (25% to 40%, cap from $150K to $500K), and made the employer paid family and medical leave credit (IRC §45S) permanent. Fleischmann's OBBB statement highlighted 'largest tax cut for families and workers.' He continues to oppose a federal PFML mandate. He also co-sponsored legislation to keep children in classrooms and protect parental rights regarding COVID-19 vaccination. No new parental support legislation co-sponsored in May-June 2026 found beyond OBBB support.

name: Anna Golladay
bio: Chattanooga progressive who previously ran for City Council. Announced February 2026.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Explicitly supports 'expanding access to quality childcare' as part of economic platform; supports 'strong schools' for rural communities; announced February 2026. No specific pre-K funding or Head Start positions stated publicly.
early_childhood_ed.details: Golladay's economy page states support for 'expanding access to quality childcare' as a cost-reduction measure for families. Her rural counties platform references 'strong hospitals, strong schools, and strong towns.' Announced campaign February 2026 with 100+ supporters at Wanderlinger Brewing in Chattanooga. She is endorsed by Vote Common Good. No specific federal pre-K, Head Start, or CCDBG expansion positions found. Her campaign frames childcare primarily as an affordability/economic issue.

child_hunger.summary: Cites grocery cost 'financial panic' for families; supports 'tackling price gouging'; no specific SNAP, WIC, or school meal positions stated. Opposes OBBB-era family harm ('care over cruelty'). Fleischmann's OBBB vote projected to cut ~$283M in SNAP from Hamilton County over a decade.
child_hunger.details: Golladay's economy platform states that 'a trip to the grocery store shouldn't send families into financial panic' and supports 'tackling price gouging' as part of making life affordable. She uses the slogan 'choosing care over cruelty' which implicitly frames opposition to OBBB-era cuts. However, no specific SNAP restoration, WIC expansion, summer EBT, or school meals policy positions were found in any May-June 2026 searches or website pages reviewed.

parental_support.summary: Explicitly supports guaranteed paid family and medical leave and expanding quality childcare. Announced February 2026. Frames as economic dignity issue grounded in her progressive faith background.
parental_support.details: Golladay's February 2026 campaign announcement and platform explicitly call for 'guaranteed paid family and medical leave' and 'expanding access to quality childcare.' Her platform positions her as a faith-based progressive arguing these are moral and economic dignity issues: 'Tennessee deserves more than a Congressperson who shows up for donors and party bosses, but disappears when working families are struggling to survive.' No specific dollar amounts for paid leave weeks/pay rates or child tax credit expansion figures found.

name: Scott DesJarlais
bio: Eight-term incumbent and physician. Faces a contested Republican primary.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: Opposes expanded federal education spending and favors state and parental control, with no support for federal early childhood education investments found. Voted NO on ARP (2021); Heritage Action 100% in 117th Congress.
early_childhood_ed.details: DesJarlais's official education page states the U.S. 'spends more per student than almost every country' yet lags on test scores, implying opposition to increased federal spending. He voted NO on ARP (2021) which included childcare and pre-K funding. He voted for OBBB (May 22, 2025, final July 2025) which included a Federal Tax Credit Scholarship Act (school choice) and enhanced employer childcare credits but no direct federal pre-K investment. He is consistently rated 100% by Heritage Action. Running for 9th term in TN-4 Republican primary against Arnold, Davis, and Jones.

child_hunger.summary: Voted NO on ARP SNAP expansions; issued press releases in February and October 2025 opposing migrant SNAP eligibility; voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill, which cuts SNAP by ~$187 billion. Issued press release headlined 'Rep. Scott DesJarlais Votes to Empower Tennessee Families and Small Businesses.'
child_hunger.details: DesJarlais voted NAY on the American Rescue Plan (Roll Call 72, March 2021). In February 2025, he praised the Trump Administration for ending migrant SNAP access, and in October 2025, he sent a follow-up letter to USDA and DHS raising continued concerns about illegal migrants potentially using SNAP. In May 2025, he voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill and issued a press release headlined 'Rep. Scott DesJarlais Votes to Empower Tennessee Families and Small Businesses in House Tax Bill,' framing the SNAP-cutting legislation as family-positive through tax cuts and business incentives.

parental_support.summary: Voted against the expanded Child Tax Credit in the American Rescue Plan and opposed paid family leave legislation, while supporting the One Big Beautiful Bill's permanent extension of the baseline $2,200 CTC. Heritage Action 100%.
parental_support.details: DesJarlais voted NAY on the American Rescue Plan, which temporarily expanded the Child Tax Credit and included childcare assistance. He earned a 100% Heritage Action score. He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill (May 2025), which makes the $2,200 baseline CTC permanent but does not expand its refundability for low-income families. No sponsored legislation or public statements supporting federal paid family leave were found.

name: Thomas Davis
bio: Republican primary challenger making his second run after a 2024 attempt.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No public position on early childhood education found; platform emphasizes returning education control to parents and states within a constitutional spending framework.
early_childhood_ed.details: Davis's issues page states that strengthening families includes 'placing the responsibility of education back to the Parents in each State,' indicating a parental-rights and state-control framework that opposes federal early childhood mandates. He frames all federal spending through a constitutional lens — only 'essential spending' aligned with the Constitution — which would encompass skepticism toward new federal early childhood programs. No press releases addressing pre-K, Head Start, or child development programs were found.

child_hunger.summary: No public position on child hunger found; overriding fiscal platform opposes federal spending programs generally within a constitutional framework.
child_hunger.details: Davis's campaign platform centers on stopping 'runaway spending,' living 'within our means,' and prioritizing 'essential spending' aligned with the Constitution. He does not address school meals, SNAP, WIC, or child nutrition programs by name anywhere on his campaign site. His stated fiscal philosophy would logically encompass skepticism toward expanded nutrition safety-net programs.

parental_support.summary: No public position on paid family leave, child tax credit, or childcare costs found; supports traditional family values and parental control over education.
parental_support.details: Davis's issues page states he supports 'strengthen[ing] families by promoting marriage, responsible fatherhood, and traditional values' and returning education decisions to parents in each state. He does not address the Child Tax Credit, federal paid family leave legislation, or childcare subsidy programs. He is a U.S. Army veteran affiliated with the VFW and American Legion.

name: Robert Arnold
bio: Filed for the Republican primary. Convicted former Rutherford County Sheriff.

early_childhood_ed.details: Robert Arnold is a convicted former Rutherford County Sheriff whose candidacy centers almost entirely on DOJ reform, law enforcement, and opposition to Jack Smith's prosecutorial record. He has made no public statements on early childhood education. His announced platform covers DOJ accountability, crime and border enforcement, and replacing what he calls a 'career politician.' No campaign website with specific policy details was publicly available.

child_hunger.details: Arnold's public campaign materials contain no references to child nutrition, food assistance programs, SNAP, school meals, or related policy. His background is in law enforcement, not social services or nutrition policy.

parental_support.summary: No public position found beyond a pro-life, pro-gun self-identification.
parental_support.details: Arnold identifies publicly as 'pro-life, pro-gun, Christian conservative' but has articulated no positions on paid family leave, the child tax credit, childcare costs, or parental rights policy. His campaign focus is on DOJ reform and public safety.

name: Harold 'Rocky' Jones
bio: Filed for the Republican primary. 24-year Air Force veteran and retired Senior Emergency Planner.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No public position found on early childhood education specifically.
early_childhood_ed.details: Harold 'Rocky' Jones, a 24-year Air Force veteran and retired Senior Emergency Planner, frames his platform around fiscal responsibility, rural healthcare, farmland protection, and affordability for working families. His campaign site mentions 'ensuring the Tennessee our children inherit remains strong, affordable, and constitutionally free,' but no specific position on Head Start, pre-K funding, childcare, or early learning programs has been publicly articulated.

child_hunger.summary: No public position found on child hunger or school meals.
child_hunger.details: Jones's 'Tennessee First' platform focuses on federal spending reduction and the national debt, which implies opposition to expanded federal food programs, but he has made no explicit statements about SNAP, school meals, WIC, or child nutrition reauthorization.

parental_support.summary: No public position found on paid family leave or child tax credit; general fiscal conservatism implies opposition to expanded federal benefits.
parental_support.details: Jones frames his economic message around stopping 'reckless spending,' reducing the national debt, and tackling inflation — a fiscal conservative posture that typically aligns with opposition to new federal entitlements. He has not addressed childcare costs, parental rights legislation, or the child tax credit directly.

name: Andy Ogles
bio: Two-term incumbent facing FEC violations and Ethics Committee scrutiny. Just $85K cash on hand (Q1 2026) — among the lowest of any U.S. House incumbent nationally. Trump-endorsed despite ongoing investigations.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Supports school choice and parental control over education; opposes federal education spending. DCCC documented approximately $10 million in federal education grants withheld from TN-5 schools under his watch.
early_childhood_ed.details: Ogles' official issues page states 'parents should decide how to educate a child best — not the Federal Government' and he supports transferring Department of Education power back to states. He supports the Tennessee Education Freedom Scholarship program. The DCCC published a page titled 'Andy Ogles Lets Tennessee Children Fail As Students in His District Miss Out on Nearly $10 Million in Funding,' citing withheld federal education grants to TN-5 schools. Ogles' office disputed the charge. No direct statements on Pre-K or Head Start were found in 2025-2026 searches.

child_hunger.summary: Voted YES on One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, July 2025), which cut SNAP by ~$187B over 10 years. DCCC accused him of 'making Tennesseans go hungry.' August 4, 2025 social media post mocked food assistance recipients: 'MAHA! If you want Uncle Sam to buy you food, you gotta go on Uncle Sam's diet.'
child_hunger.details: Ogles voted in favor of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025), which enacted the largest SNAP cuts in program history — approximately $187 billion over 10 years, removing SNAP eligibility for an estimated 4 million people and adding new work requirements for adults 55-64 and parents of children 14+. The DCCC published a direct attack page: 'Andy Ogles is Making Tennesseans Go Hungry.' His August 4, 2025 social media post stated: 'MAHA! If you want Uncle Sam to buy you food, you gotta go on Uncle Sam's diet,' signaling strong support for SNAP restrictions. Tennessee Lookout reported OBBBA SNAP cuts could cost Tennessee taxpayers over $110M annually as cost-sharing shifts to states.

parental_support.summary: Voted NO on bipartisan CTC expansion (HR 7024, 2024); voted YES on OBBBA which raised CTC from $2,000 to $2,200 but excluded lowest-income families. June 3, 2026: Ogles' official account posted 'Homosexuality has no place in America. Happy Nuclear Family Month' — deleted and blamed on a staffer after bipartisan backlash. DOJ criminal investigation dropped May 2026; House Ethics Committee probe continues. Children's burial garden GoFundMe ($25K raised) unaccounted for.
parental_support.details: Ogles voted against HR 7024, the bipartisan Child Tax Credit and worker benefits expansion bill in 2024. He then voted YES on the OBBBA (July 2025), which increased the CTC from $2,000 to $2,200 per child but ITEP analysis found 99% of children in the poorest fifth of households will receive a reduced credit or none at all. On June 3, 2026, a post appeared on Ogles' official X account reading 'Homosexuality has no place in America. Happy Nuclear Family Month,' referencing Tennessee's newly enacted Nuclear Family Month designation. Ogles deleted the post hours later, blamed a staffer, called it 'stupid' and 'hurtful,' and said the employee had been reprimanded; bipartisan condemnation followed from House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Rep. Mike Lawler, and others. Speaker Johnson called the post 'inappropriate.' The DOJ criminal investigation into Ogles' campaign finances was effectively ended when the Justice Department agreed to return or destroy seized phone evidence in May 2026. A separate GoFundMe of ~$25K raised for a children's burial garden that was never built remains unaccounted for. The House Ethics Committee investigation continues.

name: Charlie Hatcher
bio: Endorsed by former Gov. Bill Haslam and former Sen. Bob Corker. Considered the strongest Republican challenger to Ogles. $546K in FEC receipts with $214K cash on hand (Q1 2026).
photo_credit: University of Tennessee Institute of Agriculture

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific position found. Farm-first identity; as Agriculture Commissioner supported FFA and 4-H youth programs but no early childhood education policy stated.
early_childhood_ed.details: Hatcher, fifth-generation dairy farmer and former TN Agriculture Commissioner (2019-2025), retired from the commissioner role in September 2025 and launched his TN-5 Republican primary challenge to Ogles. His campaign website carries the tagline 'Pro-Gun. Pro-Life. Pro-Trump. Farm Strong.' and focuses on farming, border security, and fiscal conservatism. As Agriculture Commissioner he supported FFA, 4-H, and youth agricultural programs. No statements on Pre-K, Head Start, childcare access, or early childhood education were found in any sources through June 2026.

child_hunger.summary: No SNAP or school meals position found. Frames food security as a national security issue tied to American farming via an 'American Food Security Act' concept; no direct stance on federal nutrition programs for children.
child_hunger.details: Hatcher has proposed an 'American Food Security Act' concept that would prohibit China from owning U.S. farmland and redirect proceeds to American farmers, framing food security as a national security issue. No direct statements on SNAP, Summer EBT, school meals, or child hunger programs were found through June 2026. His farm-first identity is consistent with support for domestic food production but does not translate to a documented position on SNAP or child hunger programs.

parental_support.summary: No specific position found. Campaign theme 'Faith, Family, and Farm' implies family-values framing but no CTC or paid leave positions documented.
parental_support.details: Hatcher's campaign launch event was themed 'Faith, Family, and Farm,' and he describes himself as 'a Christian, a husband, father, and grandfather, working alongside most of my family on the farm.' No specific positions on the Child Tax Credit, paid family leave, or parental support programs were found in any sources through June 2026. His alignment with Trump and mainstream Republican conservatism suggests support for the OBBBA CTC extension but opposition to new federal mandates like paid family leave.

name: Chaz Molder
bio: DCCC top target. Has raised $1.81M total ($978K cash on hand, Q1 2026). Leads Republican candidates in fundraising. Centrist Democrat with crossover appeal in a swing district.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Has invested in Columbia education as Mayor; opposed Hillsdale charter school expansion as diverting public funds; wife is former teacher; no specific federal early childhood education proposals on campaign website.
early_childhood_ed.details: Molder, Mayor of Columbia and DCCC Red-to-Blue candidate, leads the TN-5 Democratic primary field with approximately $978K COH (Q1 2026). His campaign website covers 'Middle Tennessee Values,' 'Lowering Costs,' and 'Expanding Healthcare Access' but does not address early childhood education, Pre-K, or childcare specifically. He has cited his investment in Columbia education and his wife's background as a former teacher. He opposed the Hillsdale College charter school expansion. Affordable childcare was identified at a Middle Tennessee business forum — which Molder participated in — as among the top regional issues for families and businesses. No new direct statements on federal early childhood education programs were found in May-June 2026 searches.

child_hunger.summary: No specific SNAP or child hunger statements found. Platform pledges to lower 'everyday expenses including groceries'; criticized OBBB for cutting Tennesseans' healthcare. DCCC backing aligns him with opposition to OBBBA SNAP cuts.
child_hunger.details: No direct statements from Molder on SNAP, Summer EBT, school meals, or child hunger were found through June 2026. His campaign website states he will champion 'affordability for Tennessee families' and lower 'everyday expenses, such as healthcare, housing, and groceries.' He criticized the One Big Beautiful Bill as providing 'tax cuts for billionaires, cutting Tennesseans' health care access, and increasing the national debt.' His DCCC Red-to-Blue designation positions him in opposition to the OBBBA SNAP cuts but no explicit Molder statement attacking those cuts was found.

name: Mike Cortese
bio: Nashville Metro Council member and Belmont University adjunct professor. Has raised approximately $261K. Competing in the Democratic primary.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Co-sponsored and championed Nashville's 'Codes for Kids' childcare zoning reform legislation as Metro Council member — signed into law May 2026. The package removed a 1,000-foot zoning buffer between daycare facilities, creating ~2,750 new childcare spots in a city meeting only 56% of community need.
early_childhood_ed.details: Cortese and co-sponsor Councilmember Rollin Horton filed the 'Practical Plan to Make Childcare More Affordable' ('Codes for Kids') legislation on March 6, 2026. The package removed Nashville's 1,000-foot zoning buffer between daycare facilities and created an expedited permitting process for childcare projects. Davidson County had a shortage of approximately 2,750 childcare spots, with Nashville meeting only 56% of community need per the Nashville Early Education Coalition. The legislation garnered 24 of 40 Metro Council members as sponsors, passed all three required readings, and was signed by Mayor Freddie O'Connell in May 2026. Cortese stated: 'I'd like to get this passed ASAP, so we can get change going and get relief to families.'
